name: Song-Kol
near: There are no permanent villages on the shore. Bases: Kochkor (via Kalmak-Ashuu, ~3 h), Kyzart village (start of the horse routes), Sary-Bulak, Naryn (~90 km southeast as the crow flies, via Terskey-Torpok), and from the southwest Ak-Talaa/Baetov (Moldo-Ashuu) and Chayek/Kyzyl-Kiya (Kara-Keche).
elev: 3,016 m above sea level (map.kg, asiamountains.net, Ak-Sai, Caravanistan); Too.kg rounds it to 3,000 m.
short: Kyrgyzstan's second-largest lake, at 3,016 m amid endless jailoo (summer pasture): in summer there are yurt camps, herds of horses and flocks of sheep; in winter it is an empty, icy plain.
desc: Song-Kol is a freshwater high-mountain lake in the Inner Tian Shan between the Songkol-Too (north) and Moldo-Too (south) ranges: about 29 km long and 17–18 km wide, area ~278 km², depth up to 13–14 m (up to 22 m according to map.kg). 18 streams flow into the lake and one river, the Song-Kol, flows out. It is frozen from the second half of October–November until the end of April. There were no fish in the lake until 1959; now it has whitefish, peled and naked osman. Part of the water area belongs to the Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve (1994), and the lake is a Ramsar wetland site (2011): up to 66 species of waterfowl nest here in summer, including the Red Book bar-headed goose. The surrounding pastures (~108,000 ha) are among the country's main summer jailoos; there are no permanent settlements, and about 15 yurt camps operate from June to September. On the northern shore stands the stone mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr from the late 19th century.
guide: Stay at least one night: the highlights of Song-Kol are the sunset over the water, a starry sky without light pollution and the morning mist over the jailoo. Rent a horse from the camp hosts (about 700 som per day) and ride along the shore to the herds, try fresh kumys and watch the mares being milked. If you have 2–3 days, ride in from Kyzart via Kilemche and the Jalgyz-Karagay Pass (3,400 m) — this way the lake opens up from above, as the nomads saw it. On the northern shore, look for the mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr. Even in July there can be frost at night, so a sleeping bag and a down jacket are a must.
see: Sunset and starry sky over the lake; herds and shepherds' yurts on the jailoo; mare milking and kumys making; nesting waterfowl (bar-headed goose, cranes, swans) — a Ramsar site; the mausoleum of Taylak-baatyr on the northern shore; the switchbacks of the Kalmak-Ashuu and Moldo-Ashuu passes (“33 Parrots” — Terskey-Torpok); the Kok-Jerty cascade on the Song-Kol River (4 km below its source); in winter — the frozen lake (a winter yurt camp is set up every year — Caravanistan).
skip: You only have one day — the round trip from Kochkor takes 6–7 hours, and the whole point of the place is to spend the night. You don't tolerate an altitude of 3,000 m and night frosts well and aren't ready for outdoor facilities. You are going between October and May without winter expedition preparation — there are no camps and the passes are under snow.
diff: Medium in terms of logistics: walks around the lake are easy, but the approach is 3–4 h over high-mountain dirt roads and passes up to 3,400+ m. Horse/foot treks from Kyzart are medium (2 passes above 3,000–3,400 m, 4–6 h a day; CBT Kochkor). At 3,016 m, you need to acclimatize.
when: June–September (yurt camps operate from about late May–early June until mid-September/early October); peak season, with camps guaranteed to be open, is July–August; for peace and quiet, June and September. CBT Kochkor runs horse tours from mid-June to the end of September. The lake is frozen from the second half of October until the end of April; the passes are closed by snow in winter.
hours: An open natural area with no ticket office. Yurt camps are seasonal (Ak-Sai: June–September); in the off-season there is nobody on the shore except the winter camp (on request).
daytime: Sunset and night (stars) are the main thing; early in the morning — mist over the water and mare milking. It is best to cross the passes during the day: frost and ice are possible in the morning, thunderstorms in the evening.
how: By car: 1) Kochkor → Sary-Bulak → Kalmak-Ashuu (~3,400 m) → northeast shore — the most popular, ~3 h from Kochkor; 2) Naryn → Terskey-Torpok (“33 Parrots”) → southeast shore; 3) Ak-Talaa/Baetov → Moldo-Ashuu → southern shore; 4) Jumgal Valley/Kyzyl-Kiya → Kara-Keche → southwest. From Bishkek ~280 km (Too.kg) via Balykchy and Kochkor. On foot and horseback: Kyzart → Kilemche → Jalgyz-Karagay (3,400 m) → Song-Kol (2–3 days, CBT Kochkor), also the Tuz-Ashuu, Chil-Bel and Uzbek passes.
needcar: Yes: there is no public transport to the lake. You need an SUV/jeep with a driver from Kochkor or Naryn, your own 4×4, or a horse/hike. Do not go in a sedan (visitkyrgyzstan.org).
self: Yes, in your own 4×4 or by hiring a driver in Kochkor; no permits are needed. In summer you can find a yurt on the spot, but in July–August it is better to book through CBT/the camps 1–2 weeks ahead. Cash is a must (no ATMs or card terminals).
roadtype: Paved road to Kochkor; after that dirt and gravel over passes with switchbacks (Kalmak-Ashuu, Moldo-Ashuu, Kara-Keche); on the shore — tracks across the jailoo. High ground clearance is needed; you can puncture a tire on some sections. Check the condition of each pass for the date of your trip.
traveltime: Bishkek — Kochkor 3–4 h (marshrutka (minibus)); Kochkor — Song-Kol 3–4 h by jeep (CBT Kochkor: return transfer from Batay-Aral — 3 h); Bishkek — Song-Kol by car ~6–7 h; horse trek from Kyzart — 2 days of 4–6 h each.
stay: About 15 yurt camps around the lake (Caravanistan). Budget: $10–15 per person with breakfast and dinner (Backpack Adventures 2026; Caravanistan); mid-range $25–45 with meals (visitkyrgyzstan.org). Premium: Ak-Sai Travel Son-Kul Yurt Camp — 44 yurts for up to 90 guests, shower, electricity in every yurt, Starlink Wi-Fi; $65 (breakfast) / $75 (half board) / $85 (full board) per person in a double, single $100–115 (ak-sai.com, season June–September; booking@ak-sai.com, WhatsApp +996 770 901 616). Booking camps run by shepherds — through CBT Kochkor, CBT Naryn. Tent — free camping on the shore (there are camping spots).
net: Coverage only in places (Too.kg). The Ak-Sai camp advertises MegaCom coverage and Wi-Fi via Starlink; most shepherd camps have no connection (Caravanistan, visitkyrgyzstan.org). Beeline and O! are not confirmed at the lake. A signal can sometimes be caught on the passes.
entry: Free: no entrance ticket or eco fee for Song-Kol was found in any 2019–2026 source. You only pay for the camp, horses and transport.
transfer: Kochkor — Song-Kol by jeep: 2,500–3,500 som per car (visitkyrgyzstan.org); ~$20 per seat round trip (Caravanistan); Bishkek — Kochkor marshrutka 350 som, Bishkek — Naryn 600 som (CBT Naryn, May 2026); a 2-day tour from Bishkek — $650 for 1–2 people (Tripster).
bring: A warm sleeping bag or a fleece/down jacket (frost at night even in summer), hat and gloves, rain jacket, sun protection (UV at 3,000 m), headlamp, power bank (electricity isn't available everywhere), cash in som, altitude sickness pills/first-aid kit, shoes for wet grass, offline maps. Drink water from the lake only after boiling it.
warn: At 3,016 m altitude sickness is possible, especially if you go up from Bishkek in one day. The weather changes quickly; night frosts even in July–August; thunderstorms on the open jailoo — don't stand on high ground. The roads over the passes are dirt, with a risk of puncturing a tire, and snow at the beginning/end of the season. There is almost no mobile coverage, and no ATMs or shops. There were complaints about taxi drivers in Kyzart overcharging (TripAdvisor, May 2025) — agree on the price in advance. Dogs at shepherds' camps.
food: Kumys (fresh, straight from the shepherds in summer), beshbarmak and kuurdak made from lamb, boorsoki, kaymak (cream) and homemade jam in the yurts; at the Ak-Sai camp — national and European cuisine as a buffet. Local fish (whitefish, peled) — occasionally from fishermen.
reviews: Google Maps: 4.9/5, 382 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor (“Song Kol Lake”, Kochkor): 4.8/5, 13 reviews (2018 — May 2025; viewed 07.10.2026). Pros: incredible scenery, sunsets and stars, hospitable nomads, horse rides. Cons: a hard road, varying quality of yurts, cold nights, isolated complaints about taxi drivers in Kyzart overcharging.
p.sum: The easiest way is Bishkek → Kochkor (marshrutka 350 som, 3–4 h), then through CBT Kochkor or a private driver take a jeep to the lake via Sary-Bulak and Kalmak-Ashuu (≈85 km from the highway, 3–3.5 h; guide price ≈5,200 som per car for 4–6 people, 2026). The best experience is a 2–3-day horse trek from Kyzart village via Kilemche (from ≈15–20 thousand som per person with local guides, tours $280–440 / €). Spend the nights in yurt camps on the northern or southern shore (1,000–2,000 som with dinner and breakfast at the shepherds', $35–115 at Ak-Sai), and bring cash in advance — there are no ATMs or shops at the lake. Since September 2026 there has been a fence at Batay-Aral (southwest, Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve) — do not drive in there.

p.onsite.other.0.details: Commercial fishing on Song-Kol has been under a moratorium since 07.2023 for 3 years; recreational and sport fishing is allowed. Nets are prohibited: in June 2026 inspectors removed >5 km of poachers' nets
p.onsite.other.1.details: The water is cold (3,016 m); no beach infrastructure
p.onsite.other.3.details: Since September 2026 the Batay-Aral tract (Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve) has been fenced off with a 1 km fence: vehicle access is closed and access for people is restricted to protect nesting birds (Ramsar site)
p.onsite.camping: Tent or sleeping in the car — free, you only pay for food if you eat at the camp (Mad or Nomad, 2024). Do not drive up to the water's edge or into the fenced-off Batay-Aral bird zone (since 09.2026). In June 2026 the owners of illegal glamping sites (A-frames) were fined 200,000 som — building on the jailoo requires permits.
p.onsite.photo_spots: The Kalmak-Ashuu switchbacks on the approach, sunrise over the lake at the northern shore, herds at sunset, the starry sky; from the south — the Moldo-Ashuu hairpins, from the southeast — “33 Parrots”.

p.iti.1.title: Classic: 3 days on horseback from Kyzart

p.iti.3.title: What to combine it with
p.iti.3.plan: Kochkor (“Altyn Kol” felt), Kol-Ukok (from Kochkor), Sarala-Saz and Kilemche (horse “jailoo hopping”), Naryn and Salkyn-Tor, the Kyzyl-Korgon canyons via Kara-Keche.
p.season: May — until mid-June: snow on the passes, camps open from late May (some from 15 May). Mid-June — August: all approaches are open, the camps are working, peak in July–August, daytime up to +20…+25, around 0 at night; thunderstorms. August — festivals of national games on the jailoo. September: quieter, colder, camps close between mid-September and 20 October. October — April: the lake is under ice (~200 days), the passes are closed by snow (Kalmak-Ashuu and Moldo-Ashuu were closed as early as 2 November).
p.budget.economy: ≈4,500–6,500 som/person for 2 days: Bishkek—Kochkor marshrutka 2×350; a seat in a jeep ≈1,000–1,500 (5,200 som/car for 4–6); yurt with meals 1,000–2,000; horse for 1–2 h 250–500.
p.budget.comfort: ≈20,000–40,000 som/person: a 3-day horse tour $280–440 or a 2-day tour from Bishkek €120–$650; Ak-Sai $75–115/night with meals.
p.permits: No permit needed; no entrance tickets or eco fees. The southwestern part (Batay-Aral) is the Karatal-Japyryk nature reserve: fenced off since 09.2026, vehicle access closed.
p.access: With kids — yes, with acclimatization (3,016 m) and warm clothes; it is better to spend a night in Kochkor on the way. For older people — by jeep via Kalmak-Ashuu, comfortable camps (Ak-Sai). With a wheelchair — practically not (grass, bumps, pit toilets). With a dog it is possible, but there are aggressive dogs at shepherds' camps.
